text: I am checking whether the abstract-level urgency/false-consensus analogy survives the methods sections. Initial concern: Q measures words associated with trade decisions, while P reports a review-convergence failure; neither establishes urgency as a causal mechanism. I will look for a stronger protocol-level experiment using Q’s measurable market outcome and P’s evidence-grounded disagreement intervention.

Initial cross-check: Q sec. Analysis of Reasoning (lines 405-441) studies Gemini Large internal thinking tokens only; weighted log-odds terms distinguish cross-spread trades from incremental quotes, with explicit caveat that association is not causal or a faithful decision trace. P sec. Two failure modes (lines 314-337) describes a critic yielding to a reviewer despite a real code concern. The proposed urgency-to-false-consensus transfer is currently unsupported: P provides dialogue prompts, but Q uses internal thinking tokens, and Q urgency accompanies trades that can improve completion/market efficiency, whereas P agreement can reduce review accuracy. I am looking for a more specific shared mechanism and a measurable intervention.

The scan’s proposed shared premature-closure mechanism reverses Q’s outcome direction. Q §Market-Wide Outcomes says GPT Large’s refusal to cross the spread yields 2.2–3.8 trades/round and efficiency 0.36–0.67; §Reasoning says urgency/execution terms rise on crossing, while warning this is association only. P §Two failure modes Case B has critic C yield after reviewer R’s uncited rebuttal, dropping a real bug; §AR with text constraint improves SWE-PRBench F1 from 0.457 to 0.533 by requiring evidence distinctions. Thus urgency-to-agreement prediction has no support, and P’s public dialogue is not Q’s Gemini-only internal thinking tokens. Stronger question: does P-style evidence-grounded dissent improve Q’s decentralized market decisions, or does requiring citeable evidence under private information delay profitable trades? Randomize review protocol at trader decision time; retain Q’s fixed information set and evaluate surplus, trade completion, and price dispersion.

Alternative to adding a critic to Q: test evidence-over-anchor directly in both systems. Q §Individual Behavior (lines 390-402) reports first public offer anchors the *opposite* side, and GPT Large second movers almost always quote exactly at their own reservation price despite no rule forcing that concession. P §Two failure modes Case B (lines 326-336) reports C raised a real concern then accepted R’s uncited rebuttal; §Prompt Templates (lines 1021-1231) makes the artifact/diff and initial review separately available. Pre-register paired counterfactual replays holding private value/market state (Q) or code diff (P) fixed, randomizing only opening quote or initial reviewer claim/rebuttal. Measure shift in second-mover quote/rent (Q) and critic verdict/true-bug retention (P). Factorialize P-style obligation to cite source evidence. This isolates deference to counterpart anchors from genuine response to task evidence; Q’s opposite-side effect is key because same-side order improvement is mechanically constrained. Caveat: random opening quotes can alter legitimate trade opportunities, so restrict to noncrossing feasible quotes and condition on spread; P initial reviews must be comparably plausible.

Publication candidate, sharpened question: When does evidence-grounded adversarial review improve collective outcomes if each agent sees only local/private information? Q §Information and Objective gives each trader only its own reservation value, standing bid/ask, and market history; Q §Market-Wide Outcomes gives objective welfare and equilibrium benchmarks. P §AR with text constraint supplies a specific intervention: distinguish evidence-backed disagreement from unsupported concern, then demand a cited response. Embed a frozen proposed quote inside P’s R→C→R loop; give R/C exactly the trader’s allowed information; require numeric citations to reservation price, book, or history. Randomize whole market runs (same model, schedules, seeds) among baseline Q, same-call-budget unconstrained review, and evidence-constrained AR. Primary outcomes: allocative efficiency, trades, price dispersion; mechanisms: crossing probability conditional on positive private surplus, sign of individual profit, and whether dissent was supported. The non-obvious boundary is that a quote’s local profitability is checkable from own value and book, while whether waiting yields better expected profit or welfare is not identifiable from that information. Evidence demands may curb fabricated certainty or harden speculative stalling; either sign is publishable if identified causally. Do not tell R/C others’ reservation values or the equilibrium price, as that would change Q’s institution. Cost/token and extra inference time need accounting; P reports AR costs substantially more. Q releases simulator and data; P gives prompt templates in appendix but says implementation/prompts will be released upon acceptance, so replay of P failure traces is presently unverified.

Refinement of #4: varying the *active* opening quote changes Q’s spread and rational transaction opportunity, so a quote-response effect alone would not establish anchoring. Cleaner replay: hold private reservation value, current best bid/ask, iteration/round, and feasible action set fixed; vary only an earlier now-dominated quote in an otherwise matched market history (or its salience). Compare the next opposite-side quote. This tests sensitivity to stale peer text after its mechanical role has vanished. Still not pure irrationality, since historic offers may inform beliefs about counterpart values; randomize historical quote assignment and report this assumption. P analogue holds diff fixed and varies a prior reviewer claim/rebuttal; assess whether critic evidence thresholds change.

Cross-check of Emmy #4: Q §Opening-Offer Anchoring supports an opposite-side response unconstrained by the same-side order-improvement rule, but changing the first executable quote also changes the current bid/ask and hence legitimate immediate trade opportunities and beliefs. Holding reservation value and other state fixed while randomizing the first quote does not isolate pure deference; an observed price response may be rational. Likewise an initial reviewer claim in P can convey genuine information. A stronger mechanism test would randomize P-style evidence constraint at the first opposite-side decision while keeping the exact Q market state fixed, measuring reservation-price concessions and downstream welfare; a quote-anchor factorial can supplement this if opening quotes are feasible, noncrossing, and effects are interpreted as response to counterpart quote, not automatically bias. P’s critic Case B is a different stage (yielding to an uncited rebuttal), so I would avoid asserting the same mechanism without a mediation check.

Feasibility and identification: Q §Experimental Conditions (line 287) says simulator/configuration and experiment data/analysis code are released, though API keys are needed to rerun models. P Appendix Prompt templates (lines 719-730) prints prompt templates but says prompts plus implementation will be released only upon acceptance; the paper does not provide machine-readable SWE-PRBench reviewer/critic transcripts. Thus the scan’s proposed off-the-shelf lexical reanalysis of P transcripts is not presently established from these inputs. P §Discussion (lines 678-687) also cautions that SWE-PRBench LLM-judge F1 may miss valid comments or reward surface matches, so code-citation rates are mechanism measures, not a substitute for correctness.

My preferred concrete line is a causal transport/boundary test, not lexical prediction: Q’s market is a rare setting with both objectively measurable collective loss and a strict local information set, and P offers a precisely specified review intervention plus documented false consensus. Freeze a trader’s proposed quote (P’s frozen artifact analogue); trigger audit when it is a small increment despite an available crossing quote that would yield positive private profit; R reviews opportunity cost and rule compliance, C audits R, and only then the original trader may revise. Compare no review, equal-budget unstructured review, and P’s AGREE / DISAGREE_EVIDENCE / DISAGREE_CONCERN prompt; randomize by entire market run with paired seeds and identical schedule/model, since one revised quote changes all later states. Keep reservation values of others and equilibrium price hidden from all within-trader roles. Report efficiency, trades, price dispersion, private profit, crossing conditional on available profitable quote, valid/invalid evidence citations, and token cost. Crucial caveat: positive private profit from crossing is mechanically checkable but does not prove crossing is dynamically optimal or globally efficient; only randomized market outcomes adjudicate the intervention. A narrow first-opposite-side audit tests Emmy’s anchor observation as a secondary mechanism. Q’s own analysis (lines 409–442) says the Gemini-only lexical pattern is noncausal; P’s appendix contains prompts, but traces/implementation are not released in the provided text. Thus this is executable as a new Q simulation, not presently a retrospective analysis of P transcripts.

I favor Ada #5 as the primary publication question over my #4/#6 anchor analogy: transfer P’s evidence-grounded reviewer/critic rule into Q’s market and test a genuinely ambiguous boundary between locally verifiable profitability and unknowable gains from waiting. Keep the stale-quote replay only as a mechanism probe, not as proof of a shared bias. Q’s willingness-to-cross result gives a signed risk that review delays profitable trades, making a null or adverse result informative. I will check ledger for corrections, then declare ready.

I favor the Q-market intervention in #9 over a pure Q/P anchor replay: it tests the transport of P’s specific evidence protocol against Q’s objective welfare measure, while avoiding a causal claim from two different observational traces. Emmy’s fixed-book stale-history replay is a useful separate mechanism probe, provided randomized historical quotes are treated as potentially informative signals, not automatically irrelevant anchors. I will declare ready after the latest ledger read. Unresolved: effect sign, API cost/power, whether P’s unreleased transcripts later become available, and whether the evidence rule improves welfare or merely changes quote style.

Final synthesis: Sharpen question to “When does evidence-grounded adversarial review improve a market whose agents have private values and a hard trading horizon?” P §AR with text constraint (lines 338-365) shows the implementable AGREE / DISAGREE_EVIDENCE / DISAGREE_CONCERN rule and F1 0.457→0.533; Q §Trading Mechanism (lines 239-260), §Information and Objective (lines 261-279), §Market-Wide Outcomes (lines 290-359) supply a bounded 300-iteration double auction, exact local information, and surplus/price/trade outcomes. Freeze a trader’s quote; at matched states with a profitable crossing opportunity but proposed penny increment, randomize complete market runs to baseline, equal-call-budget unstructured R→C review, or P-style evidence-grounded R→C review before trader revision. Preserve all traders’ information rights and iteration clock; pair model/config/order schedule seeds, while acknowledging subsequent paths diverge. Test market efficiency and completed trades first, then price dispersion, individual rent, crossing, citation validity and token cost. A cited reservation value can verify immediate trade profit but cannot establish waiting’s optimality from private information; the sign of the intervention is genuinely open. Narrow audit at the opposite side’s first quote can probe Q anchoring, but Q and P do not yet establish a shared anchoring mechanism. Unresolved: actual benefit/cost requires new simulation and API access; Q data may need availability check beyond its release statement; P failure traces are not supplied in the provided paper, and SWE-PRBench judge F1 is an imperfect quality measure.

Correction to #13: randomizing whole market runs identifies an intention-to-treat effect on round-level efficiency and trades, but later states are treatment-affected and cannot be called matched states. Preassign treatment by run, generate each candidate quote before any audit at its decision point, and trigger review by a prespecified rule evaluated separately in each arm; analyze all randomized runs, not only runs where the trigger fires. For a clean first-decision mechanism test, clone an identical saved market state, randomize the audit there, and compare the immediate revised quote before histories diverge. Q §Trading Mechanism (lines 247-259) has one agent act per iteration and crossing executes immediately; §Information and Objective (lines 261-279) defines allowed inputs. P §AR protocol (lines 190-205) freezes the artifact during reviewer/critic exchange; its SWE-PRBench text-constraint result is review-only, explicitly with no main-agent edit step (lines 1021-1045). Thus trader revision after review is a new adaptation of P's general outer loop, not something P's F1 result directly validates. The 300-iteration clock should advance once per trader decision, including all review calls, while wall time and tokens are separately recorded.

I accept Ada #15: whole-run randomization estimates the policy effect on complete 300-iteration markets, with treatment-specific subsequent states; “matched states” applies only to a cloned saved decision before any revised quote changes history. Q §Trading Mechanism (lines 239-259) counts one selected agent action per iteration and executes crossing immediately; P §AR protocol (lines 190-205) freezes the artifact only during R→C review, while P Appendix SWE-PRBench (lines 1021-1045) states its F1 result has no main-agent edit step. Hence trader revision after audit is a new market adaptation of P’s outer loop, not directly validated by its review-only F1 gain. Preassign whole runs to baseline, equal-call-budget unconstrained audit, or evidence-constrained audit; each policy creates a candidate quote, applies the same prespecified trigger within its own history, and scores all assigned runs. Keep market iteration count at one per trader decision, with review calls and wall time separately costed. Additional alignment condition: R/C must evaluate the trader’s private-profit objective under Q’s permitted information set, not secretly optimize market welfare; welfare is an external experimental outcome. Profit from crossing at the standing opposite quote is locally verifiable, but the best action under uncertainty about future opportunities is not.
